claims.text: Replacing portions of heavy HEA elements with Al or Ti can decrease alloy density.
Controlled substitution of heavy elements with lightweight elements can preserve a homogeneous solid-solution microstructure.
A homogeneous solid solution fosters nanoscale dispersion strengthening.
The proposed homogeneous microstructure enables a continuous passivating Al2O3- or Cr2O3-containing oxide layer to form along grain boundaries.
Chromium addition can promote a dense Al2O3/Cr2O3 layer and improve oxidation resistance at 900°C.
Retaining oxide-forming constituents allows rapid formation of a protective oxide that mitigates corrosion and high-temperature degradation.
Retained key alloying elements form strengthening phases.
The optimized microstructure permits mechanical strength and environmental durability to be achieved simultaneously.
Chromium and molybdenum must remain above a critical concentration for the proposed balance of strength, corrosion resistance, and oxidation resistance.
Increasing molybdenum content can raise corrosion potential and lower corrosion current density.
An FeNiCuAlCr alloy exhibits low oxidation kinetics at 900°C and resistance to localized corrosion in 3.5% NaCl.
A conventional CoCrFeNiMn baseline has higher density, a mixed-phase solid solution, and lacks the optimized lightweight composition.
At an optimal substitution level, a lightweight HEA will retain strength, corrosion resistance, and oxidation resistance comparable to the higher-density baseline while having lower density.
Substitution beyond a critical level will reduce one or more of mechanical strength, corrosion resistance, or oxidation resistance.
Loss of sufficient strengthening and passivation-forming elements will increase corrosion current density or destabilize the high-temperature protective oxide.
A lightweight AlTiVNb HEA film has been synthesized for investigation of its microstructure, mechanical properties, and corrosion resistance.
